**Template.** These runbooks and agents are examples. They cover the full path to a production build and must be modified to meet each customer's specific requirements. The customer or their partner connects them to their own systems, identity, data and governance in their environment.

Turn cart friction into consent-aware recovery planning without touching a shopper or cart.

Analyzes anonymous synthetic cart patterns, drafts neutral channel sequences, compares margin-aware incentive concepts, and reviews aggregate conversion scenarios.

**Why try it:** It helps growth and digital teams pressure-test recovery ideas while preserving consent, margin governance, and activation controls.

## Problem Statement

Recovery programs can become slow, generic, over-discounted, and difficult to evaluate when journey friction and margin tradeoffs are unclear.

## Solution Summary

A portable planning agent converts anonymous commerce-style records into review briefs that marketing teams can refine before approved systems handle any contact or offer.

**Blueprint role:** Anonymous recovery planning

**Capabilities:** Anonymous abandonment analysis; Consent-aware campaign draft; Margin-aware incentive scenarios; Synthetic conversion review. See [responsibilities and trust boundaries](2.Architecture.md).

## Business Outcomes

- Clearer diagnosis of cart friction
- More disciplined review of channel and incentive options
- Stronger consent and activation governance

Claims are qualitative; synthetic demo figures are not customer results or performance commitments. See the [claims policy](../../solutions/README.md#claims-policy).

## Target Users

| Role | Need |
| --- | --- |
| Marketing Manager | See where the anonymous synthetic cart journey breaks down and what needs margin-aware review. |
| Digital Marketing Lead | Outline a consent-aware draft sequence without sending or scheduling anything. |
| Growth Manager | Compare incentive scenarios for approval and separate benchmarks from planning estimates. |

## In Scope / Out of Scope

### In scope

- Summarize anonymous synthetic cart count, value, exit pages, device mix and review state, highlighting workflow friction.
- Show draft channels, review timing, neutral subject concepts, the consent gate and benchmark assumptions.
- Compare fixed cost impact, modeled lift and net-value incentive scenarios, each an option for approval.
- Report packaged aggregate recovery metrics with benchmarks separated from forecasts and assumptions named.

### Out of scope / approval boundary

- No shopper identification or contact; only anonymous synthetic carts and aggregate metrics are used.
- No outreach sent or scheduled, no retargeting, and no offer created or applied.
- No cart change, stock reservation or purchase completion.
- No live commerce feed or claim of live recovery performance; metrics are fixed synthetic evidence.
- No Outlook or Teams activation; that needs separate approval and implementation.
- No workshop publishing; publication remains a separate authorized step.

## Qualification Checklist

- [ ] Is a Microsoft Copilot Studio target environment, with an approved publisher prefix, available for the cart-recovery build?
- [ ] Can the team use the Copilot Studio plugin with PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer, or follow the manual upload lane?
- [ ] Is an approved aggregate, read-only commerce analytics feed available without shopper-level identity?
- [ ] Has the customer defined the consent and campaign review workflow that must approve any campaign or incentive?
- [ ] Will any future write require authenticated tools, authorization checks, explicit human approval and an audit log?
- [ ] Is publication held for separate approval after replaying every locked cart case against the reviewed instructions, knowledge, skills and model?
- [ ] Have governance, telemetry, support and success measures been agreed for production recovery planning?

## What Actually Goes Wrong

- **shopper-identification:** Anonymous cart records are stitched to a real shopper or contact identity.
- **draft-sequence-activated:** The draft recovery sequence is sent, scheduled or retargeted before consent and approval.
- **scenario-issued-as-offer:** An incentive scenario is issued as a coupon, discount or reward.
- **benchmark-as-performance:** Benchmark open and conversion rates are presented as live performance or a forecast.
- **pressure-messaging:** Draft subjects add urgency pressure or availability claims.
- **unknown-cart-id:** An unknown cart identifier is approximated from another cart.

See [state and recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery).
